Author: Sanjay Kumar Singh

sentences.text: Applicant :- Sushil Kumar Bhurjji
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others Counsel for Applicant :-
Kameshwar Singh Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Kuldeep Singh Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.

Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned Additional Government Advocate representing the State and learned counsel appearing on behalf of the first informant / complainant.
By means of this application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C., applicant Sushil Kumar Bhurji, who is involved in Case Crime No. 146 of 2021, under Sections 363, 376, 506 IPC, Section 5/6 POCSO Act and Section 3(2)(5) SC/ST Act, police station Kalinjar, district Banda, seeks enlargement on bail during the pendency of trial.
As per prosecution case, in brief, informant, who is father of the victim, lodged the first information report of this case on 27.12.2021 against unknown person with the allegation inter alia that on 27.12.2021 at about 09:00 A.M., his daughter aged about 17 years had left for school but she did not come back yet.

sentences.text: It is argued by learned counsel for the applicant that the victim was major on the date of incident and she was consenting party with the applicant, therefore, it is not a case of rape but a case of consensual relation between the parties concerned.
The applicant does not have any criminal history to his credit.
Lastly, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant that there is no chance of the applicant fleeing away from the judicial process or tampering with the prosecution evidence.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 05.01.2022 and in case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and cooperate with the trial.

On the other hand, learned A.G.A. for the State as well as learned counsel for the informant vehemently opposed the prayer for bail of the applicant by contending that as per high school marksheet of the victim, her date of birth is 10.08.2004, therefore, on the relevant date of incident,
she was minor aged about 17 years and 04 months.

They also pointed out that the victim in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. has also stated inter alia that the applicant has committed misdeed with her and from his relation, she became pregnant.
Hence, bail application of the applicant is liable to be rejected.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and examined the matter in its entirety, I find that as per the statement of the victim, she is minor and is a student of Xth standard whereas the applicant is a married person aged about 30 years and he is distant uncle of the victim.
Not only this but the applicant also used to teach children in the house of the victim.
It is also not disputed that the victim became pregnant from the forceful relation of the applicant.
The offence is heinous in nature.
A rapist not only violates the victim's personal integrity, but leaves indelible marks on the very soul of the helpless female.
In this case, a hapless girl had been ravished by the accused.
The act of sexual assault induces trauma and horror for any girl or regardless of her social position in the society.

Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case as well as keeping in view the submissions advanced on behalf of parties, gravity of offence, role assigned to applicant and severity of punishment, I do not find any good ground to release the applicant on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is rejected.
It is made clear that the observation contained in the instant order is confined to the issue of bail and shall not affect the merit of the trial.

However, the trial Court is directed to make an endeavour to conclude the trial expeditiously without granting any unnecessary adjournment to either of the parties in accordance with provisions of Section 309 Cr.P.C.
Order Date :- 20.4.2023 Shubham  Sushil Kumar Bhurjji vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118553159/
